description: Shared behavioural fixture for the comment masker that both suites carry: `strip_comments` in ontology_suite/sketch/bind_analysis.py, and `stripComments` in src/triplify/bindAnalysis.ts. Both must return exactly `expected` for each `input`, and `expected` is always the same length as `input` -- comments are blanked to spaces rather than removed, so every offset reported afterwards still indexes the real document. Kept identical in both repos; test_strip_comments_parity.py and stripCommentsParity.test.ts run their own port against their own copy, and compare the copies when both checkouts are present. The cases are maintained by hand, not generated from either implementation: a generated fixture only ever restates what the code already does, and would have agreed with both ports on the day they were both wrong.

cases.name: a trailing comment is blanked
cases.why: The defect both ports shipped: a line-oriented scan that only skipped a line *starting* with `#` left this comment fully in scope, so the rename rewrote the note explaining the rename.

cases.name: a whole-line comment is blanked
cases.why: The case the old line-oriented scan did get right.

cases.name: a fragment IRI keeps its local name
cases.why: `#` is the fragment separator in almost every RDF namespace. A naive `#`-to-end-of-line strip truncates the term and every CURIE after it.

cases.name: a comment after a fragment IRI is still blanked
cases.why: The IRI must close the exemption, not extend it to the rest of the line.

cases.name: a hash inside a double-quoted literal is not a comment
cases.why: A term named in an sh:message is text, not a remark.

cases.name: a hash inside a single-quoted literal is not a comment
cases.why: Both quote styles are legal in Turtle and SPARQL.

cases.name: a line of a triple-quoted literal may begin with a hash
cases.why: The reason this reads the text straight through rather than line by line: a multi-line literal's quoting state does not survive a split.
cases.input:
:a rdfs:comment """line one
# still literal
line three""" .
cases.expected:
:a rdfs:comment """line one
# still literal
line three""" .

cases.name: an escaped quote does not end the literal
cases.why: Ending the literal early would put the rest of the line back in scope and blank a real term as though it were a remark.

cases.name: a TARQL IRI template survives with its comment blanked
cases.why: The shape both ports exist to handle: a CURIE built inside a literal is a real term reference, and the remark beside it is not.

cases.name: text with no comment is returned unchanged
cases.why: The identity case. A masker that alters uncommented text is worse than no masker.

cases.name: an unclosed literal swallows the rest of the input
cases.why: Malformed input must not crash and must not be quietly repaired. Both ports read the rest of the text as literal, so nothing is blanked and a `#` that was probably meant as a comment stays in scope. That is a guess either way; what matters is that the two ports guess alike, since a file this broken should be failing its parser, not its masker.

cases.name: a bare less-than is not an IRI
cases.why: `<` only opens an IRI when a well-formed one follows, so the `#` here is an ordinary comment.

cases.name: a comment at end of input needs no newline
cases.why: The end-of-text branch: the search for the line ending finds none, and the comment runs to the end of the text.

cases.name: a CRLF line ending keeps every later offset true
cases.why: The CR sits between the comment and the LF, so it is inside the blanked span and both ports space it over. That costs nothing -- the newline stays where it was and the length is unchanged, which is all a mask owes its caller -- but it is worth pinning, because a port that stopped one character earlier would shift every offset after it.

cases.name: empty input
cases.why: The degenerate case, pinned because both ports index into the text.

cases.name: a hash immediately after an IRI closes
cases.why: No space between `>` and `#`: the exemption ends at the bracket.
